requirements.text: If the relevant guidance is not yet in a usable state, make sure it is appropriately prepared so it can be applied
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 195 AND state = 'published'
assumptions: KB-0000195 (knowledge 195) is the only article for product 128 (Palo Alto Networks PA-3220) and is retired on the seed
the policy allows only published articles to be linked, so 'prepared so it can be applied' means state published

requirements.text: link the relevant knowledge article ... for resolving
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_kb_id = 528 AND case_id = 1 AND knowledge_id = 195 AND used_as = 'resolution'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; this is the only case_knowledge row the task creates
case 1 is Elizabeth Chase's (user 801, contact 123) only case on product 128 that is both new and critical
knowledge_id 195 added: the request names the relevant article, which the benchmark check leaves open, and 195 is the only article for the case's product
used_as resolution: the request links it 'for resolving', and the policy uses resolution for an article useful to resolve the case

requirements.text: link the relevant knowledge article ... regarding Palo Alto Networks PA-3220
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_id = 1 AND knowledge_id IN (210, 227, 244, 263, 264)
assumptions: articles 210, 227, 244, 263 and 264 are published and carry 'PA-3220' in their titles but cover the Variant products (140, 152, 164, 176), not product 128 on the case

requirements.text: progress the SLA to begin investigation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 1 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: case SLA 1 is case 1's critical response SLA (definition 1), paused on the seed; case 1 has two SLA records and beginning investigation resumes both

requirements.text: progress the SLA to begin investigation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 2 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: case SLA 2 is case 1's critical resolution SLA (definition 6), paused on the seed; case 1 has two SLA records and beginning investigation resumes both

requirements.text: progress the SLA to begin investigation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1 AND state = 'in_progress'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: beginning investigation moves the case from new to in_progress, a transition the policy allows
case 1 is Elizabeth Chase's (user 801, contact 123) only case on product 128 that is both new and critical

requirements.text: Also, let them know about the changes
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 734 AND case_id = 1 AND email = 'elizabeth.chase32@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; this is the only notification the task creates
'them' is the reporter, Elizabeth Chase (user 801), at her user email
type update kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and consistent with telling her about changes to the case

notes:
The two independent passes agree on all seven requirements (article 195 published; case_knowledge 528 linking it to case 1 as resolution; no PA-3220 Variant article linked to case 1; case SLAs 1 and 2 in_progress; case 1 in_progress; notification 734 of type update to Elizabeth Chase on case 1) and on all five dispositions (kept); no disagreements.
The benchmark checks read a single value and compare it with 'contains' (stage, state, type); each requirement tests the same value as an exact count, which is equivalent because no other value in use for these columns contains the expected one.
Elizabeth Chase's other PA-3220 cases (5, 10, 14, 17) are not new, so they fall outside 'the new critical case'.
The acting user, Joanne Simpson (user 4), is an active manager who is not in case 1's assignment group 4 and is not its assignee; the policy lets managers reassign cases across groups and contribute to knowledge management as reviewers, and the benchmark expects the updates, so updating case 1 and publishing article 195 are treated as allowed.
Article 195 has internal visibility; the request does not ask that the customer can read it, and preparing it so it can be applied needs only the published state, so visibility is not tested. The notification's knowledge reference and status are not tested: neither the request nor the policy fixes them.
